decisions.reason: The old phrase each test function used specified neither a testing domain nor an output map. The repair declares positive measurable input representatives, a map into real locally integrable representatives, maximal absolutely integrable tests and a nonzero declared testing subspace. The weak identity is an admissibility condition, not an existence or uniqueness theorem; arbitrary symmetric collision measures and the entropy-only test branch are preserved.

The Definition correctly allows every nonnegative width and asserts no asymptotic narrowness. Only the display title overpromised narrowness; removed that adjective without restricting widths or changing the Definition. The block-limit supplier use separately assumes delta_N/N tends to zero and a sufficient lower width.

The Lebesgue Definition explicitly withholds the measure property; product/Tonelli and change-of-variables therefore needed the complete-measure theorem and its Countable Choice premise. Added the precise measure, sigma-finiteness, box, product-completion and Riemann-to-Lebesgue bridges, plus integral order/linearity and compact uniform continuity. Rechecked Gaussian moments, factorial asymptotics and the fixed-block tail estimate; defined the zero-probability normalization branch without changing any limit.

F2 attributed unit modulus to definitions, although the correct modulus corollary was already declared and stated in F1. Corrected F2 to that corollary. Checked the rank-one spectrum, offdiagonal Cesaro bound and limiting two eigenvalues; the argument and Example are unchanged.

The two definitions did not supply the bounded-Borel integration and linearity used in step 4.1. Added the actual order, simple-integral agreement and L1 linearity suppliers and derived the boundedness/error estimates. Checked compact graph hull, fiber attainment, arbitrary-measure approximation, lower semicontinuity, convexity, d+1 support and finite Jensen. Statement unchanged.

F1 confused the mean energy integral with the barycenter-constrained infimum. This is a nonfatal nomenclature/restatement defect: A1 and both proof steps already use the unconstrained objective explicitly. Corrected that distinction, supplied nonnegative integral order and simple-integral agreement, and checked finite integrability. Countable additivity forces positive mass on some [1/n,1), giving positive energy for every law; point masses at 1/n approach zero.
